summary.intent: Get a real phone call working for the Soony hackathon demo (alert call to a teammate's phone with approve/escalate decision recorded on the dashboard), at minimal or zero cost, ideally with an ElevenLabs voice agent on top.
summary.outcome: Found that the new Twilio trial cannot buy numbers or verify caller IDs via API, but provides a shared trial From number (+49 158...) that works for keypad TTS calls. Configured .env and the escalation policy, changed escalation.py to serve the call script via a URL endpoint, restarted the service and placed test calls; the final call status and recorded decision were checked but the result is not shown in the transcript.

repo: Secrets and personal phone numbers go in .env and a gitignored data/alert-policy.json; they must not be pasted in chat, and decision logs should have phone numbers masked.
The code has a 'call provider' interface, so adding another provider (e.g. OpenAI Realtime, Telegram channel) is a contained change.
Twilio needs to fetch the call script from a public URL, so the service exposes an endpoint serving the TwiML call script (added in escalation.py).

code.finding: Edited so the Twilio call passes a URL to a service-hosted call script instead of inline TwiML, because the trial account rejected/ignored the inline parameter; line numbers not given in the transcript.

workflow: Twilio's new trial (Nov 2026) cannot buy numbers, cannot place caller-ID verification calls, and the console funnels to an upgrade page; the signup number is auto-verified and calls originate from a shared trial number, only within the signup country, with TTS and keypad (no Stream/Dial/Record).
Trial limits: 75 free minutes, 10 min per call, up to 5 verified numbers; ElevenLabs voice agent needs an owned Twilio number so requires upgrade.
Azure free credits cannot be used for ACS phone numbers, even on pay-as-you-go; not a viable path.
Reading the actual docs page the user linked corrected an earlier wrong conclusion that an upgrade was unavoidable; check primary docs before declaring blockers.
No MCP servers for Twilio/ElevenLabs were available, so API calls via scripts were used.
